question: What is the primary operational feature of a day care centre?

options.A: Clients reside permanently within the facility grounds
options.B: Care is provided exclusively during severe medical emergencies
options.C: Children stay overnight throughout the entire week
options.D: Clients return home to their families every evening

explanation: Day care centres provide daytime supervision only, allowing clients to return home to their families at the end of each day. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why are day care centres considered important community health resources?

options.A: They offer permanent housing for abandoned elderly individuals
options.B: They provide safe supervision and social support while caregivers work
options.C: They serve as boarding schools for school-aged adolescents
options.D: They replace the need for primary healthcare clinics entirely

explanation: These centres support families by caring for dependents safely during working hours, promoting both child development and adult well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which objective is a primary focus of a child day care centre?

options.A: Promoting early socialization and cognitive play

explanation: Child day care focuses heavily on early childhood development through structured play, social interaction, and cognitive activities. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h2)

question: How do day care services benefit family caregivers directly?

options.A: By offering financial loans for business start-ups
options.B: By reducing caregiver burnout through reliable respite
options.C: By permanently taking over full parental responsibilities
options.D: By providing free housing facilities for the whole family

explanation: Reliable daytime care gives parents and family caregivers time to work or rest, preventing severe physical and emotional exhaustion. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the main focus of an adult day care centre?

options.A: Offering specialized infant feeding and sleeping routines
options.B: Preparing young children for primary school entry
options.C: Conducting major surgeries for elderly patients

explanation: Adult day care centres focus on keeping elderly or disabled clients safe, socially engaged, and compliant with their daily medications. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h3)

question: A working mother needs daytime care for her two-year-old toddler. Which facility type is most appropriate?
explanation: A two-year-old falls into the toddler category, making an infant and toddler nursery the correct setting for age-appropriate physical care and safety. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why are day care centres particularly vulnerable to infectious disease outbreaks?

options.A: Clients live permanently inside the building
options.B: Groups of vulnerable individuals gather in close contact
options.C: Staff members are not allowed to wash their hands
options.D: Sanitation guidelines forbid the use of soap and water

explanation: Gathering young children or frail adults in enclosed spaces makes it easy for germs to spread rapidly among them. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is a key safety requirement for storing cleaning chemicals in a day care centre?

options.A: Storing them securely out of reach of children
options.B: Placing them next to food preparation counters
options.C: Keeping them unlocked on low shelves for easy access
options.D: Mixing them with drinking water for cleaning

explanation: Toxic chemicals must always be stored securely away from children to prevent accidental poisoning or chemical burns. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: What should day care staff do when they notice a child showing signs of a developmental delay?

options.A: Scold the child for failing to meet peer standards
options.B: Ignore the sign until the child starts primary school
options.C: Withhold meals until the developmental milestone is met
options.D: Note the observation and refer the family for assessment

explanation: Early identification and referral help ensure children get the professional support they need for developmental delays. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is proper nutrition especially critical for children attending day care centres?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any physical exercise routines
options.B: It replaces the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: It guarantees that children will never catch a common cold
options.D: It supports both physical growth and cognitive development

explanation: Balanced nutrition provides the essential energy and nutrients required for growing bodies and developing brains during early childhood. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility during a routine visit to a day care centre?

options.B: Managing the financial accounts of the facility

explanation: Community health nurses check immunization records to verify that all children are up-to-date on vaccines, protecting the group from outbreaks. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h6)

question: How does the community health nurse help prevent the spread of infectious disease in a day care facility?

options.A: By closing the facility permanently at the first sign of illness
options.B: By forbidding parents from visiting the facility
options.C: By prescribing strong antibiotics to every child present
options.D: By educating staff on hygiene and infection recognition

explanation: Educating day care workers on proper hygiene and early symptom spotting empowers staff to stop infections before they spread. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is a common management challenge in day care centres?

options.A: Complete absence of any government regulations
options.B: Too much space for very few enrolled children
options.C: High staff turnover and inadequate funding
options.D: Excessive numbers of trained medical doctors on site

explanation: Many day care centres struggle with financial constraints and frequent changes in caregiving staff, which can disrupt service quality. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why is maintaining proper staff-to-child ratios important for quality assurance?

options.A: It reduces the need for cleaning the facility every day
options.B: It ensures every child receives adequate supervision and attention
options.C: It allows staff members to take long holidays during work hours
options.D: It guarantees higher financial profits for the facility owners

explanation: Appropriate ratios prevent overcrowding and ensure caregivers can adequately supervise and respond to each child's needs. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h7)
